newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says US merger won't affect fleet plans.
newsitem.headline: KLM says US merger won't affect fleet plans.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Monday the announced merger of U.S. planemakers Boeing and McDonnel Douglas would have no immediate effect on its aircraft buying plans.
"The merger will not have any direct effect on KLM's purchasing plans," spokesman Peter Wellhuner said.

He said it was too early to forecast the long-term impact of the merger on KLM's purchasing strategy. "It will all depend on whether the aeroplanes (manufactured by the new combine) will meet the criteria set (by KLM)," he said.

The Dutch airline currently has three Boeing 747-400 combi aircraft on order, but the delivery of one has been put back to after the year 2000 as part of KLM's recently announced Focus 2000 restructuring programme.
The other two are due for delivery in April 1997 and September 1998 respectively.
KLM also has two Boeing 737-400s on order for delivery in September and October next year and two Boeing 767s for delivery in February and May.
It is further due to take delivery of a McDonnel Douglas MD-11 in May 1997.
